definitions.gloss: without flattery; honestly; in all sincerity
definitions.explanation: A phrase used before a compliment to emphasize that it is genuine and not just polite flattery.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで、おいしいです。
examples.english: Honestly, it's delicious — I'm not just saying that.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで、⟦{素晴|すば}らしい→素晴らしい：01119_subarashii⟧⟦プレゼン→プレゼン：05505_purezen⟧でした。
examples.english: Without flattery, it was an excellent presentation.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで⟦{言|い}います→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歌|うた}→歌：02179_uta⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}います→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I'm being completely honest when I say her singing is really good.

notes:
USAGE:
お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで is used to preface a genuine compliment, assuring the listener that the praise is sincere. Japanese social culture involves frequent compliments (⟦お{世辞|せじ}→お世辞：07023_oseji⟧), so this phrase explicitly sets them aside.

FORMS:
- ⟦お{世辞|せじ}→お世辞：07023_oseji⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}き→抜き：23505_nuki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ — slightly more formal variant
- ⟦お{世辞|せじ}→お世辞：07023_oseji⟧じゃ⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧ — casual variant (not flattery, but...)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで + praise/compliment
- お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧... (speaking without flattery...)
